subject: Mediflow: canary latency spikes — fallback & pinning exception request
messages:
From: Alex Han <alex.han@mediflow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@mediflow.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent latency during canary — urgent remediation request

Hi Ben / Laura,

We started a small A/B canary for checkout autosuggest yesterday and saw two ~300-600ms p99 latency spikes lasting ~4–6 minutes each, visible in our NewRelic traces. This is outside the 99.9% latency target in our contract and it impacted a subset of live traffic.

We understand A/B testing carries some risk, but we need an operational guarantee that production traffic can automatically fail back to the last known-good model/version and pin to the stable variant if the canary breaches thresholds. Without that behavior, we can't safely run progressive launches.

Can you advise whether Redwood can: 1) enable automatic fallback/pin to the previous version for the canary route, 2) set a hard latency threshold (we proposed 250ms p99) to trigger the fallback, and 3) provide a short-term SLA carveout for this canary window while we validate the changes?

I attached a small telemetry sample and a cropped trace (mediflow_latency_samples.zip). Procurement has looped to coordinate any formal exception paperwork.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Han
Platform Engineering
Mediflow Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Han <alex.han@mediflow.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency during canary — urgent remediation request

On Wed, Jun 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM Alex Han <alex.han@mediflow.com> wrote:
> We started a small A/B canary for checkout autosuggest yesterday and saw two ~300-600ms p99 latency spikes lasting ~4–6 minutes each...

Alex — thanks for sending this over and for the telemetry sample. Sorry you hit that window.

Short answer: yes, we can implement an automated fallback + version pin during the canary, and we can also process a conditional SLA exception for the short validation period — with a couple of operational guardrails. Proposed immediate steps: 

- Configure the canary route with an automated failover rule: if p99 latency > 250ms for a rolling 5-minute window OR error rate > 0.5%, route 100% of traffic to the previously pinned version.
- Apply a temporary pin to the prior model variant for 30 minutes post-failover to prevent flapping; manual unlock required thereafter.
- Enable aggressive KV cache warm on the canary nodes and pre-warm top N prefixes based on your recent traffic sample.
- Telemetry alerting: we’ll send a PagerDuty event to Mediflow on first trigger and publish a brief incident summary to the shared Drive link.

Operationally, to approve the SLA carveout we need: an exec-level confirmation from Procurement, a filled SLA exception form (I attached a draft), and sign-off from our onboarding/ops (looping Karthik). If Procurement agrees immediately we can enact the routing change within the hour for the remainder of your validation window.

Attached: canary_policy_draft.md (policy we’d apply).

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Han <alex.han@mediflow.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency during canary — urgent remediation request

Ben / Laura — quick tech + ops read.

I reviewed the telemetry sample and can confirm the traces show cold KV misses on several heavy prefixes during the spike windows. Our runtime supports the failover and pin behavior Ben described; implementation details:

- Rollout policy: traffic-shift policy with automatic 100% swap back on threshold breach (p99 > 250ms OR errors > 0.5%) using our smart-routing engine.
- Pin semantics: pinned version will remain active for 30 minutes after an automatic fallback; we can make that configurable per-customer.
- Safe-mode: when pinned, we will disable experimental quantization variants and force the stable kernel selection to avoid runtime variance.
- Telemetry: we will instrument an audit log entry for every automatic fallback and expose a trace id for your SREs.

Requesting formal approval to enable this behavior for Mediflow’s canary window. If Procurement needs the SLA exception paperwork, Ben can coordinate — I’ll prepare a short checklist for the ops team to validate pre- and post-change.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Han <alex.han@mediflow.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency during canary — urgent remediation request

Thanks everyone — reviewed and OK to proceed with conditions.

Approval summary (conditional):

1) Redwood will enable an automatic fallback + 30-minute pin on the Mediflow canary route with thresholds: p99 > 250ms (5-minute rolling) OR errors > 0.5%.
2) The pin will block autoswap to experimental quantized variants while active.
3) Mediflow signs SLA exception form (attached: sla_exception_form.pdf) agreeing to the validation window and accepting that the temporary carveout applies only during the designated canary timeframe.
4) Redwood will provide an incident summary and the audit log (trace ids) within 2 business hours after any fallback event.
5) If any fallback occurs more than twice in a 24-hour period we will escalate to a joint post-mortem and pause further canaries until resolved.

Ben — please coordinate procurement signatures and schedule the policy flip; Marissa, please own the post-deploy telemetry checklist and confirm KV pre-warm is in place prior to the canary restart.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
